title: certify projected helper three-cycle minimum of thirteen XORs
head: 0980a7c266532b42ccda3d77bf61b5cf18be9054
body:
For any finite number of arbitrary dirty helpers and one dirty target, a raw-identity scalar XOR word needs exactly 13 gates to induce a projected three-cycle of three helpers while fixing the rest. The package gives an attaining word and a computer-assisted lower bound: a target-write rank argument and coefficient restriction reduce every hypothetical word of length at most 12 to five registers, where two complete radius-six searches exclude it.

Both representations contain 1,421,983 states and agree on every endpoint; both translated intersections are empty. Local normal and optimized Python 3.12.14 runs reproduced the certificate, semantic controls and credited predecessor fixtures. A legal same-length witness mutation was rejected. The registered replay runs the full optimized calculation in about six seconds here, using about 321 MiB peak memory. The dimension-independent reduction remains written mathematics, not a kernel proof.

This extends the general projected-defect handoff in #1396 under the scoped claim #1503. The existing range theorem, write-count observation, elementary loops and SWAP witness remain credited to Gareth Davidson (@bitplane), PR #1420, with earlier lineage from @woklerx, PR #1105. Prepared by Andrey Mas with substantial GPT-6 Pro research/checker assistance through ChatGPT; Codex handled coordination, packaging and separate local replay. No independent human review is claimed.

The result concerns the unit scalar XOR/helper contract. It supplies no paid-frame admission, complete recursive moment, new multiplication exponent or selected-frontier change. It changes only the new research package and includes source pins, explicit replay instructions, limitations and an open formalization question.

Validation: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/projected-three-cycle-minimum`.
limits: Metadata and source identity only. Checks require source/command/coverage review; no green-badge inference.
